From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-09T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Intermittent 504s during peak window (Mar 8) — infra triage notes

Monica / Stephanie — triage notes below after reviewing our ingestion and runtime traces for us-west-2.

What I checked:
- API gateway logs (14:30–15:00 UTC) for 504/502/5xx spike
- Inference runtime traces for redwood-llm-v2 for the same window\- Autoscaler/slot allocation events

Findings:
- No systemic 504 or 5xx spike at the gateway level. We see 2 occurrences of transient 503 from one edge node, but both have upstream retries and are not correlated with higher-layer runtime OOMs or kernel failures.
- Runtime traces show a small latency bump (p50->p95) for redwood-llm-v2 between 14:42–14:46 UTC on two hosts, but the tail latency remained within the customer's published SLO.
- The request IDs Sam provided (req_7b12f9e4, req_7b12f9f1) are present in our logs; both returned 200 on our side with token outputs. No internal errors recorded.

Repro attempt:
- Ran a focused replay with identical payloads to the prod routing (us-west-2, hosted) and couldn't reproduce 504s.

Next steps / asks for the customer:
- Can the customer capture a HAR or SDK debug logs for one failing request (steps attached: how-to-capture-har.txt).
- If they can re-run with request logging enabled (SDK flag) for a 15-minute window, that would capture full round-trip headers.
- Share any client-side proxy or CDN details — sometimes client-side retries stack up and produce client-side 504s while our backend succeeded.

Attachment: runtime-trace-snippet.txt (excerpt) — includes host timestamps and the two host IDs where latency bumped.

Conclusion: At this time we cannot confirm a Redwood-caused outage. Evidence points to transient edge retry behavior and client-side retry/backoff factors as possible contributors. Recommend capturing HAR to conclusively determine whether the 504 was generated by the client, our gateway, or an intermediate proxy.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
SRE — Infra, Redwood Inference
--- Attachment: runtime-trace-snippet.txt (text) ---

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sam Keller <sam.keller@finexcorp.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-09T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Intermittent 504s during peak window (Mar 8) — update and closure steps

Hi Sam — quick update from our side after infra triage. Short version: we couldn't reproduce a service-side 504 for the request IDs you provided. Our logs show those IDs completed successfully and we only see two transient 503s at an edge node that recovered via upstream retry.

Actionable next steps for you (to conclusively close):
1) Capture a HAR or SDK debug log for a failing request (see attached how-to-capture-har.txt). This will show whether the 504 is returned by the client, a proxy, or our gateway.
2) If you have client-side proxies or CDN (CloudFront, etc.), please share the edge logs for the same timestamps.
3) Consider short client-side retry/backoff if you haven't already. Our recommendations: exponential backoff starting at 100ms with jitter, max 3 retries.

We'll keep monitoring your project for the next 72 hours. If you can provide a HAR or a fresh failing request with headers, we'll re-open and perform a deep trace (including kernel-level logs). If no further incidents are observed, we'll mark this as 'no issue found' on our side.

Appreciate the quick report — apologies for the disruption to your demo. Let me know if you'd like us to schedule a short screen share to capture a HAR together.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
